decisions.executionNote: Approach the blue nut with the left arm, lifting and gradually orienting downward while keeping the right arm parked.

Lower to the blue nut, close fully, and make a short test lift. Retention will be checked visually.
Blue nut is visible between the fingers. Lift and carry it above its blue bolt in the left workspace, then begin a cautious descent.
Seat the blue nut over the visible bolt tip and begin a slow clockwise tightening stroke with the gripper closed.
Release the blue nut in place, reset the wrist counterclockwise without gripping, then regrasp for another tightening stroke.
The blue nut has tipped beside the bolt rather than staying threaded. Withdraw open and inspect for a recovery grasp.
Turn the open jaws to avoid the neighboring bolt and lower over the tipped blue nut for a recovery grasp.
Refine the blue-nut centering from the wrist image, close fully, and lift to check its recovered orientation.
Lower the recovered upright blue nut slowly toward the bolt, checking insertion before applying any more rotation.
The bolt is still offset beneath the nut. Lift slightly, translate the nut toward the bolt, and lower gently without turning.
Refine the blue nut-to-bolt offset from the wrist view, then lower six millimeters to test seating while keeping the grasp closed.
The recovered nut appears tilted. Lift clear of the bolt and cautiously adjust its pitch about the grasp center before attempting insertion again.
Correct the pitch direction while bringing the held blue nut back above its bolt at clearance height. Keep the grasp closed.
Reorient the sideways blue nut with a larger controlled pitch change, compensating the wrist position to keep the nut elevated near the bolt.
Finish uprighting the blue nut and bring it above the blue bolt, allowing for the link-to-grasp offset. Check the resulting alignment before release.
Tracking was interrupted near contact. Release the blue nut at its current placement and withdraw vertically from the latest measured pose to inspect safely.
Recover from the interrupted withdrawal with smaller increments, returning the empty left gripper toward a downward-facing pose at safe clearance.
Bridge the outstanding tracking residual with a small intermediate pose, settle, then slowly relieve wrist pitch and raise the empty gripper.
Continue the now-tracking withdrawal to a vertical open-gripper inspection pose above the blue parts, preserving the elbow-up branch.
Lower the open gripper directly over the displaced blue nut, accounting for the longer link6-to-finger offset, and inspect before closing.
Center the blue nut between the open fingers, close fully at tabletop grasp height, and lift for a fresh visual alignment check.
Translate the retained blue nut over the bolt axis estimated from the head view, then descend ten millimeters without twisting.
Apply a slow clockwise seating stroke to the blue nut with only three millimeters of downward feed, keeping the gripper closed.
Set the misoriented blue nut down clear of its bolt before switching to the untouched purple pair; no fastening is assumed.
Correct the rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Lift open and move above the purple nut while resetting wrist yaw.
Lower over the upright purple nut for a clean grasp, while moving the right arm to a separate elevated receiving pose.
Center and grasp the upright purple nut, then lift it. Keep the receiving arm safely on the right at an elevated staging pose.
Correct the rejected row; no preceding motion occurred. Carry the purple nut to the center and finish the receiving wrist orientation.
Lower the purple nut to its original tabletop grasp height at the center, then release for a staged handover.
Withdraw the left gripper from the released purple nut, then approach the center from the right with ample arm separation.
Correct the rejected tensor; no motion occurred. Clear the left arm and approach the center nut from the right at a safe height.
Center the right gripper over the staged purple nut, lower to pickup height, and close fully without moving the parked left arm.
Lift the purple nut with the right gripper closed and carry it into the right workspace, maintaining its upright orientation.
Carry the retained upright purple nut above its matching bolt and lower slightly, reserving final alignment for the wrist view.
Lower the upright purple nut twelve millimeters at the estimated bolt axis, without rotating, to check whether the bolt enters the bore.
The purple bolt appears against one side of the bore. Relieve contact, shift six millimeters inward and four rearward, and reseat gently.
Begin a slow clockwise purple-nut tightening stroke with two millimeters of axial feed; keep it gripped and inspect engagement before releasing.
Release in place and reset the wrist with the jaws open, then regrasp for the next tightening stroke. Check whether the purple nut remains upright on the bolt.
The purple bolt cap is now centered in the nut. Apply another controlled clockwise tightening stroke with a small axial feed.
Reset the right wrist counterclockwise with the gripper open, keeping the seated purple nut in place, then regrasp.
Continue clockwise tightening of the aligned purple pair with a gentle two-millimeter downward feed.
Open the right gripper, reset the wrist without unscrewing the purple nut, and close again for another tightening stroke.
Continue tightening the centered purple nut clockwise with a small downward feed and the right gripper fully closed.
Release and withdraw from the tightened purple pair, then move above the red nut without disturbing either assembly.
Approach the red nut vertically with the right gripper open, correcting the small wrist tilt before the pickup.
Center the red nut using the right wrist image, close fully at pickup height, and lift to verify retention.
Carry the retained red nut above its matching bolt, with extra clearance over the completed purple pair.
Lower the upright red nut toward the bolt without twisting; check bore alignment at the end of the descent.
Make a small lateral correction toward the red bolt and lower twelve millimeters slowly, keeping the nut upright and closed in the gripper.
The red nut tilted during seating. Stop feeding downward, release the constraint, and withdraw slightly to inspect whether it settles onto the bolt.
The red nut settled upright with the bolt centered. Regrasp at the seated height and begin controlled clockwise tightening.
Correct the rejected tensor; no motion occurred. Finish the red tightening stroke and release while moving the open left gripper above the blue nut.
Reset the open right wrist and regrasp the red nut. Lower the left gripper over the blue nut for a new recovery grasp.
Grasp and lift the blue nut well clear of the table for orientation recovery, while continuing a clockwise red tightening stroke.
Rotate the sideways blue nut toward upright about its elevated grasp center, compensating the link-to-finger offset. Reset the red wrist open, then regrasp.

Release the blue nut onto the clear staging patch and withdraw rather than forcing the low horizontal pose. Reset the right wrist open and regrasp the red nut.
Return the empty left gripper to a vertical inspection pose above the staged blue nut. Apply one further slow clockwise tightening stroke to the red pair.

Lower the reoriented blue nut toward the empty staging patch and release just above the surface, without forcing the near-horizontal gripper into the table.

Return the open left gripper to a vertical view over the released blue nut, preserving the current elbow-up configuration and leaving the completed right-side pairs undisturbed.

Finish returning the left gripper to vertical above the blue nut's observed staging position, keeping it open and clear of the table.

Refine the upright blue nut's centering, grasp fully, and lift straight up. Re-estimate the bolt axis before translating or inserting.
Move the upright blue nut over the revised bolt-axis estimate with a small clearance lift, then approach slowly. Keep the other two pairs undisturbed.
